links.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT-4.0 smoking cessation treatment recommendations versus physician decisions, by case complexity
links.effect: Overall concordance 67.1%; 32.9% inappropriate. Inappropriate recommendations in 81.5% of chronic disease cases and 77.8% of regular medication cases (p=0.021, p=0.030).
links.quote: ChatGPT-4.0 provided inappropriate recommendations in 81.5% of cases involving chronic diseases and 77.8% of cases involving regular medication use (p = 0.021, p = 0.030, respectively).

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating the concordance and appropriateness of ChatGPT-4.0 recommendations compared to physician decisions for smoking cessation using electronic patient records, without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
